thread:
Elaine: FYI seeing a surge of PCIe AER corrected errors + NVLink link flaps in rack23, started ~2026-03-18T09:57Z. A few training pods OOM'ing after retries. Need quick triage.

Zack: grabbing dmesg and nvidia-smi now. Initial log snippet from gpu-02:
```
[ 1357.987654] pcieport 0000:03:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e7
[ 1357.987655] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, PID=4012, GPU=1(0a02)
[ 1357.987656] nvlink: link 0 degraded (retransmit count rising)
```

Maya: ECC readouts show single-bit spikes and a few DBE on gpu-02 and gpu-11. Snapshot:
```
GPU 1: Volatile Single Bit ECC errors: 68
GPU 1: Volatile Double Bit ECC errors: 1
```

Priya: Impact: nightly-train jobs slower, throughput down ~18% on rack23, some batch jobs falling back to smaller batch size which increases iteration count. Not yet customer-facing but wasting reserved capacity.

Dan: Kernel/driver changes in that rack recently?

Zack: We did a host kernel roll to 6.5.2 on that rack Friday; driver nv 535.100. Also swapped a top-of-rack NIC last week (but that shouldn't touch GPU PCIe lanes).

Elaine: Please avoid changing AER masks cluster-wide. Last time we did that we missed underlying HW faults.

Zack: I'll cordon gpu-node-02 and gpu-node-11 and evacuate pods. Commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-02.rack23
kubectl drain gpu-node-02.rack23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=90
``` 
Also increasing batch backlog capacity in us-west-2 to absorb jobs.

Maya: Running quick PCIe checks on-host:
```
sudo lspci -s 03:00.0 -vvv | grep -i aer -A4
sudo ethtool -S eno1 | grep -i error
cat /sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:1c.3/aer_stats
```
lspci shows 'Corrected error' counters incrementing, aer_stats shows <correctable> rising.

Priya: Any thermal or power anomalies? Rack sensors: inlet 23.5C, PSU voltages stable. No anomalies in PDUs.

Dan: Could NVLink bridge cable be bad? We had similar in rack14 where reseating fixed flaps.

Zack: I can try a soft fallback: reconfigure pod scheduling to avoid NVLink peer pairs (set affinity to single-GPU jobs where possible) so cross-GPU NVLink traffic reduces. Patch applied to scheduler for affected node pool.

Elaine: Spell it 'Elaine' - also add hw-oncall. @hw-oncall please triage riser and NVLink bridge during next window.

hw-bot: HW-ONCALL assigned: Carolyn

Carolyn: I'll be onsite tomorrow 09:30 PT. Plan: reseat NVLink bridge, reseat GPU in riser slot 2. If errors persist we'll RMA GPU. Bring spare nvlink bridge and riser.

Zack: Uploaded diagnostics: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/2026-03-18/rack23/diagnostics_gpu-02.tar.gz

Priya: Cost impact: spinning up extra in us-west-2 estimated +$2.2k/day. Finance notified if >36h.

Dan: Post-incident follow-ups: correlate kernel roll window + first AER timestamp, check if any NIC firmware changes, and capture full aer_stats trend.

Elaine: Action items:
- Zack: keep nodes drained and route jobs away (in progress)
- Carolyn/hw: on-site reseat + swap parts (scheduled)
- Infra: roll back kernel on a single canary node in rack23 to 6.4.x to test
- Telemetry: preserve aer_stats, dmesg, nvidia-smi outputs to S3 path above
- Priya: track cost burn and escalation threshold

Zack: noted. If we see p99 customer latency spike, I'll escalate immediately.

Maya: Quick note: don't suppress Xid 31/43 in containers; it hides HW hurt signals.

Elaine: thanks all, I'll own postmortem. Keep updates concise here.
